judgments.reasoning_cat1: Clear removal right vested in the electing Member, though it bears the duplicated number 'Section 6.6'.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It dovetails with Sections 5.5(ii) and 6.1 on who elects and fills each seat; the duplicate numbering is the only relational wrinkle.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Short agency statement, definite.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with Sections 6.1, 6.8 and 7.6.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A fourteen-item list of reserved actions ending in open-ended terms like 'any material capital expenditure' and 'any material liability or obligation'; item (iii)'s exception for reimbursing 'DMSA for initial capital contributions' is drafted for one side only.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: That distribution carve-out cuts against Section 9.1 (distributions in proportion to Percentage Interests), Section 4.3(i) (return of contributions pro rata with all-Member consent) and Section 9.2 (Board sets amounts); other sections also cross-refer to this list as 'Section 6.9'.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Detailed and conventional officer provisions with no ambiguous operative term.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 6.8(x) requires unanimous Board approval for officer employment contracts while this section lets a Board majority remove officers and fix salaries — a modest tension.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'General and active management of the business' is a broad grant, but the exceptions are spelled out.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It sits against Section 6.1 (Board manages) and Section 6.8 (President may not take listed actions without unanimous Board approval), which qualify but do not contradict it.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Standard substitution provision, definite.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with Sections 7.1 and 7.2.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Ordinary secretarial duties, clearly stated.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with the 'Secretary' definition and Sections 2.1(iii) and 2.6, which give the Secretary filing and Schedule A duties.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Conventional treasurer duties with nothing to construe.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Fits Sections 6.8(xi) (deposit banks) and 10.1-10.2.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Short agency statement, definite.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Parallel to Section 6.7 and consistent with Section 7.2.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'A fiduciary duty of loyalty and care similar to those of directors and officers of business corporations organized under the Maine Business Corporation Act' imports a whole body of law by the vague measure 'similar to', and the opening 'except to the extent provided herein' is undefined in reach.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 12.3 says the Agreement's provisions replace duties otherwise existing, and Section 12.7 expressly relieves DMSA of its fiduciary duties as a Director, so the scope of this duty is contested by other operative text.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Simple pro-rata allocation of Profits and Losses.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with Sections 8.2, 9.1 and the Percentage Interest definition, though Section 15.3 liquidates by Capital Account balances.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Subsection (ii) refers to how Members 'shared Interest Profits and Losses', a garbled phrase, and (iv) says intentions 'are intended', a drafting slip.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It defers to Section 8.1 and the Treasury Regulations without contradicting other provisions.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Standard §704(c) language.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with Sections 4.4 and 8.1-8.2.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A single pro-rata rule, clear on its face.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 6.8(iii) bars distributions without unanimous Board approval except to reimburse DMSA, and Section 4.3(ii)(b) promises profits by 'Membership Interests', so the distribution regime is not fully harmonised.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: One sentence giving the Board total timing discretion — clear, though wholly discretionary.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It leaves distributions to a Board majority while Section 6.8(iii) requires unanimous Board authorisation for any distribution, a direct clash.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Narrow legality limitation, definite.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Its 'notwithstanding any provision to the contrary' opener harmonises it with Sections 9.1-9.2 and 4.3(i).

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Standard withholding mechanics; the internal citation 'pursuant to this 9.4' is slightly mangled.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with Articles VIII and IX.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: It requires books 'in accordance with generally accepted accounting principles... and, to the extent inconsistent therewith, in accordance with this Agreement', and refers to 'the Certificate', a term the Agreement never defines.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: 'The Certificate' evidently means the 'Articles' as defined in Article I, and Section 10.2's accrual mandate must be read with the cash-basis Net Cash Flow definition.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Short and definite: accrual method, consistently applied, GAAP.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The Net Cash Flow definition expressly requires determination 'in accordance with the cash receipts and disbursements method of accounting', which cannot be squared with a blanket accrual mandate 'for both financial and tax reporting purposes'.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Designation and notice duty are precise, including the ten-day deadline.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with Section 11.2 and Article X.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: One-line tax classification, definite.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with Article VIII allocations and Section 11.1.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Standard statutory limited-liability recital, clearly worded.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with Sections 12.4, 15.5 and 4.5.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The provision is visibly incomplete: after subsection (i) the text jumps to a dangling fragment ('professional or expert competence and who has been selected with reasonable care...') with no subject, so a whole reliance limb is missing.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Exculpation for good-faith acts must be read against Section 7.7's corporate-style fiduciary duties and Section 12.3, which the missing text was presumably meant to bridge.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'To the extent that they restrict the duties and liabilities of a Covered Person' leaves the reader to identify which provisions do the restricting.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 7.7 imposes Maine Business Corporation Act-style loyalty and care duties while this section replaces duties existing at law or equity, and Section 12.7 removes DMSA's duties outright — the three do not harmonise cleanly.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A carefully bounded indemnity with express good-faith and gross-negligence carve-outs; the exclusions are stated, not left to inference.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 17.11 confers rights only on Members and Managers, yet indemnity here runs to all Covered Persons including employees and Affiliates.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Advancement mechanics are clear and conditioned on an undertaking to repay.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It cross-refers correctly to Section 12.4, though like it runs to Covered Persons beyond Section 17.11's beneficiaries.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The sentence breaks off mid-clause ('against any liability that may be asserted') so the insurable scope is simply missing from the text.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Insurance is permissive and does not clash with Sections 12.4-12.5, but the truncation leaves its relationship to indemnification unstated.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The sentence 'and the Company the income or profits derived therefrom' is missing a verb, and LSB's restraint turns on the undefined phrases 'such services' and 'to the extent it relates to the business' — an exclusivity obligation of indeterminate scope and duration. The one-sided drafting (DMSA free to compete, LSB bound) compounds the ambiguity.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It expressly relieves DMSA of the fiduciary duties Section 7.7 imposes on Directors and Section 12.3 addresses, and its reference to 'the business' must be read against the Section 3.1 purpose clause, which describes both a narrow Spanish-language media object and any lawful activity.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Consent must come from 'the LLC', a party the Agreement never defines (the defined entity is the 'Company'), the confidentiality obligation has no time limit, and 'all efforts and actions undertaken by them for the Company' is an extraordinarily broad confidentiality subject beside the enumerated Proprietary Information list.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 12.7 permits DMSA to pursue competing ventures while this section bars all use of Company information, and the consent mechanism ('the LLC') has no counterpart in the Board/Member approval machinery of Sections 5.1 and 6.8.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Admission conditions are precise (unanimous approval, execution, naming on Schedule A).
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with the 'Additional Members' definition, Section 15.1 and Section 16.3.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Detailed tax-allocation mechanics tied to §706(d); dense but definite.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with Article VIII and Section 13.1.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Without complying with the terms of this Agreement' is circular and identifies no particular restriction.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The applicable restrictions live in Article XVI (and Section 14.3 for pledges), so this section only points outward, and Section 16.8 lets the Board waive them.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Clear invalidation of non-conforming assignments, with a typo in the Article reference.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Article XIV contains only Sections 14.1-14.3 while the real transfer machinery is in Article XVI, so the reference to 'violation of this Article XIV' is under-inclusive.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Flat prohibition on pledge without all Members' written consent — definite.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 16.8 lets the Board unilaterally waive 'any transfer restrictions contained in this Agreement', which would override this all-Member consent requirement.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: One-line rule, clear.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with Sections 13.1 and 15.2.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The list includes 'retirement, resignation, expulsion' of a Member without defining expulsion or providing any expulsion mechanism, and 'death' is inapt for the corporate Member.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 5.4 forbids a Member from resigning at all, yet resignation is listed here as a dissolution trigger — the two cannot both be given full effect.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'The Members shall continue to distribute Interest Profits and Losses' is garbled, and 'a reasonable time... for the orderly liquidation' is elastic.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Liquidating proceeds go out by Capital Account balances here while Sections 8.1 and 9.1 allocate and distribute by Percentage Interests, and winding up is given to the Board although Section 15.3 says the Members distribute.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Termination condition is stated definitely.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with Sections 2.3 and 15.3.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Clear no-recourse formulation.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with Sections 4.3, 4.5 and 12.1.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Each transfer of Interests shall be made on Schedule A' treats a schedule as a transfer register, an unusual formulation but an intelligible one.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 2.1(iii) has the Secretary maintain Schedule A and says revisions are not amendments, which fits, but Article XVI's transfer conditions must be satisfied first.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Transfer' is defined expansively with a single carve-out for revocable proxies, and the section refers to 'the restrictions on transfer set forth below' without saying which of Sections 16.3-16.8 are meant. The forfeiture consequences (deemed not voted, no distribution) are stated clearly.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Its breadth overlaps Sections 14.1 and 14.3, and Section 16.8 allows the Board to waive all of it.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Two clear alternative conditions for a valid transfer.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with Sections 13.1 and 16.2.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The provision breaks off mid-sentence ('the Company and the other Members shall') and cross-refers to Sections 16.9, 16.10 and 16.11, none of which exist in the Agreement. It has no ascertainable operative content as drafted.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Article XVI stops at Section 16.8, so this waiver clause dangles against a set of provisions the instrument never contains — an irreconcilable gap in the transfer scheme.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: An opinion 'in form and substance satisfactory to the Board or the President' plus waiver 'for good cause' are both standardless discretionary tests.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It gives the President a unilateral waiver power that sits oddly with Section 16.8, which requires a duly adopted Board resolution for any waiver of transfer restrictions.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: It refers to 'the number of LLC Votes', a term the Agreement never defines (the defined term is 'Member Votes'), and the allocation sentence ('If the aggregate Interests offered to be purchased exceeds the number to be transferred') is awkwardly expressed; the timing mechanics, by contrast, are precise.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Treating Interests as countable units strains the unitary 'Interest' definition in Article I, and Section 16.8 permits the Board to waive this right of first refusal altogether.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Such additional rules and regulations as it deems expedient' is open-ended but expressly bounded by consistency with the Agreement.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The 'not inconsistent with this Agreement' limit reconciles it with Article XVI and Section 17.10.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Notwithstanding anything to the contrary' plus 'if and to the extent that the Board deems a waiver... to be in the best interests of the Company' is a wholly discretionary override.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It empowers a Board majority to dispense with Section 14.3's all-Member pledge consent and Section 16.6's right of first refusal, which the Members bargained for — a direct conflict with those provisions.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Delivery methods are enumerated but the section does not say when each is effective beyond 'deemed to have been given when received'.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It keys the Company's address to Section 2.5, which the Board may change at any time, and Members' addresses to Schedule A, which the Secretary may update — workable but loosely linked.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The sentence is convoluted ('shall not prevent a subsequent act, which would have originally constituted a violation, from having the effect of an original violation') and omits the usual statement that the earlier failure is not itself a waiver.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It coexists with Sections 17.3 and 16.8's express waiver machinery without contradiction.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Standard cumulative-remedies boilerplate.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with Section 17.2 and the indemnification articles.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Short binding-effect clause, qualified by 'to the extent permitted by this Agreement'.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: That qualifier ties it to the transfer restrictions in Articles XIV and XVI, so no conflict arises.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Conventional construction rule.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Its promise that Section references 'refer to corresponding provisions of this Agreement' is strained by the references to non-existent Sections 6.9, 16.9, 16.10 and 16.11.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Standard severability language with a stray period but no change in meaning.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Applies generally; no conflicting provision.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Standard counterparts clause.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with Sections 2.1(ii) and 13.1, which contemplate counterpart execution.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Pertaining to the subject matter hereof' is the usual limiting phrase and is not defined, but the clause is conventional.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Schedule A and any Articles of Organization sit outside the four corners, and Section 2.1(iii) says Schedule A revisions are not amendments, which raises a mild integration question.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Maine law chosen clearly, with conflicts principles excluded.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The Company's operations and principal place of business are in Massachusetts (Section 2.5), but that is a choice-of-law fact, not an internal contradiction.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Unanimity plus writing and execution — precise as drafted.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 2.1(iii) declares Schedule A revisions (which alter Percentage Interests and Member Votes) not to be amendments, allowing changes to core economics without the unanimity this section requires.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Nothing expressed or implied' with the sole exception of 'the Members and Managers' is a tightly drawn no-third-party-beneficiary clause.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Sections 12.4 and 12.5 grant indemnity and expense-advance rights to all 'Covered Persons' — employees, agents and Affiliates who are neither Members nor Managers — which this section would deny them.
